content:
The Lines, Angles & Triangles chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Lines, Angles & Triangles tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Lines, Angles & Triangles

Angle relationships, triangle properties, congruence and similarity, the Pythagoras theorem and area.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Angle sum of a triangle = 180°; exterior angle = sum of remote interior angles.
  • Pythagoras: hypotenuse² = base² + height².
  • Similar triangles: sides in proportion, areas in the square of that ratio.
  • Congruence tests: SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Using the side ratio (not its square) for areas of similar triangles.
  • Assuming similarity without a valid AA/SSS/SAS criterion.
  • Mislabelling the exterior angle.

quiz.title: CAT Lines, Angles & Triangles Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CAT-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: Two angles are complementary. If one angle measures 35°, what is the measure of the other angle?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Complementary angles sum to 90°.
Step 2: Other angle = 90° - 35° = 55°.
Answer: 55°

questions.q: Two angles are supplementary. If one angle measures 110°, what is the other angle?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Supplementary angles sum to 180°.
Step 2: Other angle = 180° - 110° = 70°.
Answer: 70°

questions.q: In triangle ABC, angle A = 65° and angle B = 75°. What is the measure of angle C?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Angle sum property: A + B + C = 180°.
Step 2: 65° + 75° + C = 180°.
Step 3: C = 180° - 140° = 40°.
Answer: 40°

questions.q: Two straight lines intersect at a point. One of the four angles formed measures 72°. What is the measure of the vertically opposite angle?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Vertically opposite angles are formed when two lines intersect.
Step 2: Vertically opposite angles are always equal.
Step 3: The vertically opposite angle also measures 72°.
Answer: 72°

questions.q: The exterior angle of a triangle is 115°. One of the two non-adjacent interior angles is 50°. Find the other non-adjacent interior angle.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Exterior angle theorem: exterior angle = sum of two non-adjacent interior angles.
Step 2: 115° = 50° + x.
Step 3: x = 115° - 50° = 65°.
Answer: 65°

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. If one alternate interior angle measures 48°, what is the other alternate interior angle?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, alternate interior angles are equal.
Step 2: The other alternate interior angle = 48°.
Answer: 48°

questions.q: What is the measure of each interior angle of an equilateral triangle?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal and all three angles equal.
Step 2: Sum of angles = 180°, so each angle = 180° / 3 = 60°.
Answer: 60°

questions.q: In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle (the angle between the two equal sides) is 40°. What is each base angle?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In an isosceles triangle, the two base angles are equal.
Step 2: Sum of all angles = 180°. Let each base angle = x.
Step 3: 40° + 2x = 180° → 2x = 140° → x = 70°.
Answer: 70°

questions.q: A right triangle has legs of length 3 cm and 4 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Apply Pythagoras theorem: hypotenuse² = 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25.
Step 2: Hypotenuse = √25 = 5 cm.
Answer: 5 cm

questions.q: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is 13 cm and one leg is 5 cm. What is the length of the other leg?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Pythagoras theorem: leg² + 5² = 13².
Step 2: leg² = 169 - 25 = 144.
Step 3: leg = √144 = 12 cm.
Answer: 12 cm

faq.q: How do areas of similar triangles compare?
faq.a: As the square of the ratio of corresponding sides — if sides are 2:3, areas are 4:9.
SSS, SAS, ASA (and AAS), and RHS for right triangles.
